facts.text: With no arguments Program.cs writes the usage line to stderr and returns exit code 1.
Any exception escaping a verb is caught at the top level, its Message written to stderr, and the process returns 1.
Verb and option validation runs before the dispatch switch, so a rejected option opens no store and reads no file.
at: Reject unknown options and valueless options before the switch

facts.text: An unrecognised verb falls to the default arm, which reprints the usage line and returns 1.
VerbSpec returns value flags, boolean flags and the index where flag parsing starts, which is 2 for dossier compile because the sub-verb is args[1].
The dump entry in the VerbSpec table accepts --entity-subjects as a boolean flag beside --source, --subject, --kind, --split and --tag.
A verb missing from the VerbSpec table is not validated, which keeps init, version and mcp on their exact previous behaviour.
at: A verb missing from the table is not

facts.text: ValidationError reports that an option requires a value when it is the last token or when the next token is another known flag of the verb.
ValidationError skips a token that does not start with a double hyphen or that is exactly two characters long, leaving positional ids alone.
ClosestFlag offers a did-you-mean suggestion only when the closest flag is within an edit distance of 2.
When two candidate flags are equally close, ClosestFlag keeps the one that compares ordinally smaller.
FlagDistance also measures each hyphen-aligned suffix of the known flag, so a dropped qualifier such as --mode still points at --budget-mode.
ValueAfter scans from index 1 and stops one short of the end, so a flag in the last position yields null rather than reading past the array.
ValuesAfter collects every value that follows a repeated flag and returns an empty list when the flag is absent.
ParseLong accepts plain digits only, rejecting K or M suffixes and negative signs, and treats 0 as unlimited.
ParseCursor rejects any value that is not a non-negative integer and names the offending flag in the error.
Program.cs builds the changes request with ParseCursor for --since and ParseInt for --last, so the two cursors are parsed by different helpers.
post reads the request body from stdin when --file is a single dash.
post prints the response to stdout, writes each item error to stderr, and still returns 0.
verify collects ids from every argument after the verb but skips any token beginning with a double hyphen, so --require-current is never an id.
publish rejects --budget, --budget-mode, --depth, --facts and --index-max-tokens when --format jsonl is set.
publish requires --max-files, --max-file-bytes and --max-total-bytes to come with --format jsonl.
publish defaults --assets to detail for markdown and to files for JSONL.
publish records its own CommandLine, quoting any argument that is empty or contains whitespace or a single quote.
publish writes any warnings to stderr, prints a summary object to stdout, then prints the compliance report when one is present.
serve falls back to port 8787 when --port is absent and announces the loopback URL on stderr.
serve blocks on a ManualResetEventSlim that Ctrl+C releases after cancelling the default termination.
mcp takes the writer name from the DOSSIER_AGENT environment variable when the client sends no clientInfo.name.
dossier compile reports the token estimator and used_tokens on stderr so stdout carries only the dossier body.
dossier compile defaults --format to json and rejects any other value than json or markdown with exit code 1.
The dossier verb prints its own compile usage and returns 1 unless the second argument is exactly compile.
AppVersion falls back to the assembly version's first three parts and then to 0.0.0 when no informational version is attached.
AppVersion truncates the version string at the first plus sign, dropping any sourcerevision suffix.
AppVersion.Current is a static property initialised once by Read, so the version is computed a single time per process.
at: public static string Current { get; } = Read();

facts.text: dump refuses to run without both --source and --subject, printing one message naming both flags and returning 1.
dump collects every --tag value into Tags, so one file can be ingested under several tags.
search prints the string returned by Ops.Search, so the rendering of hits lives outside Program.cs.
check reads the drafts file from stdin when --drafts is a single dash, before parsing it with ParseDrafts.
On success retract prints a RetractedOutput holding the id and the literal word retracted.
retract reports fact not found with the requested id on stderr and returns 1 when the id does not exist.
import passes --db to the DossierStore constructor, so the rebuild can target a database other than the default.
ParseInt throws an ArgumentException naming the flag and the offending value rather than returning a default.
ParseLimit always words its failure as --limit must be an integer, even though it is called only for --limit.
